submission.justification: Simulation scans over 50–300 um (unirradiated, 100k events each) show Sensor-T1 has the best resolution at every thickness: about 5.8–6.2 um across 125–200 um (6.9 um at 50 um, 8.4 um at 300 um). Sensor-T2 is about 9.3–12 um and Sensor-T3 is about 13.6–19 um. These numbers match the 2025 summary (6.0/9.0/14.0 um at 150 um). Between 125 and 200 um the T1 curve is flat within the run-to-run scatter (~0.2–0.3 um), so I chose 150 um. It is a central point that matches the earlier study and avoids going thicker than needed. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: The radiation-suitability constraint has NOT been checked. None of the project documents give fluence or radiation-hardness data for any candidate, and the simulation tool models only unirradiated sensors. T1's resolution depends on large signal sharing, and charge trapping after irradiation may reduce that sharing, so its advantage could shrink at end of life. This recommendation is therefore conditional. Before the Q2 market survey closes, the collaboration should confirm the innermost-layer fluence and get irradiated test-beam or simulation results for T1. If T1 fails, the fallback should be whichever candidate is shown to be radiation-hard. Note that a 3D-electrode design like T3 is often chosen for rad-hardness, but that is not established in these documents.
